These are far above the $120 price, which suggests many targets predate the selloff. Treat with caution.

summary: Oracle trades at about $120, roughly 52% below its 52-week high of $249 and near its 52-week low of $109. Operations are strong: Q1 FY27 revenue grew 30%, OCI grew 121%, and RPO is $664B. Funding is the problem. Free cash flow was about -$5B in the quarter, capex is huge, $20B of stock was sold through the ATM, and backlog depends heavily on a few AI customers. At about 15x guided FY27 EPS of $8.10 the stock looks fairly valued with a wide range, so we stay Neutral with low conviction until the cash-flow path is clearer. Note that the analyst targets I found ($238-$265) look stale against the current price.

valuation.method: Earnings-power check: guided FY27 non-GAAP EPS $8.10 x 13-20x (software-peer to hyperscaler range) = $105-$162; midpoint about 16.5x = $134. Analyst targets ($238-$265 average, some sources) look stale against a $120 price, so I gave them little weight. DCF skipped because FCF is deeply negative and capex path is unknowable from sources read.
valuation.note: Peer data is thin: I found no consistent, dated trailing P/E or EV/Sales for peers. Some cells are null. ORCL forward P/E is computed from price and guided EPS; aggregator pages show about 26x on a different EPS basis. Peer figures come from undated sources.
